rulings.item: Order of ORACLE-VALUE-CACHE against a faster mp square root: Nat::isqrt by Newton division is 55-61 % of a shard
rulings.recommendation: Rewrite Nat::isqrt division-free (reciprocal square root Newton, or Zimmermann's Karatsuba square root) first: no stale-value risk; then measure what a value cache still saves

informational: mathtools consts.rs caches pi/ln2/ln10/2-over-pi at the largest precision a process asked for and returns it truncated: fixed-precision approximations depend on call history (shard split, order); correctly rounded results do not unless a bound is wrong, but undecided-at-cap and the random lines' ulp tally can. A value cache must store decided results only.
complex_f128 shard: recomputing ln 10 as the precision grows is 10.8 % of the shard, paid in every shard process
